evidence.scope: Computational orthology; reason R1725 stays closed, not used for R1726.

evidence.claim: S. cerevisiae CPT1 manifests relative specificity for CDP-choline and CDP-dimethylethanolamine; EPT1 uses CDP-ethanolamine, -monomethylethanolamine, -dimethylethanolamine and -choline; the cpt1 ept1 double null is viable.
evidence.scope: Abstract read; S. cerevisiae enzymology, applied to Y. lipolytica by orthology.

evidence.claim: In vivo the CPT1 gene product makes 95 % of PC via the CDP-choline pathway and EPT1 5 %; CPT1 is implicated in PC synthesis from choline released by PC turnover.
CPT1 catalyses the final step of the CDP-choline route to PC; the route adds net PC only when exogenous choline is present and otherwise recycles choline from PC turnover.
S. cerevisiae psd1 psd2 double mutants are auxotrophic for ethanolamine.
evidence.scope: Abstract read; S. cerevisiae; supports keeping R1725 closed.

evidence.claim: Y. lipolytica phospholipid biosynthesis 'is still poorly understood'; no CPT1 / EPT1 experiment reported.
evidence.scope: Full text read (Szczepanska et al. 2022); absence of Y. lipolytica CPT1 / EPT1 work rests on one standard web search, not an exhaustive review.

notes.r1726_cpt_open_evidence: YALI1C15420g = YALI0C10989g, KEGG K00994 CPT1 ortholog (orthology only); S. cerevisiae CPT1 makes 95 % of CDP-choline-route PC in vivo and is relatively specific for CDP-choline (PMID 7961735, 1847919).
